strategyPoints: Tire management will be critical on this abrasive surface. We're expecting to see at least one pit stop per car, possibly two.
The pit window here is relatively short, so teams will need to be precise with their timing to avoid losing valuable time.
Fuel consumption will be a factor, especially in the closing stages of the race. Teams will need to keep a close eye on their levels.
The long straights offer good opportunities for overtaking, so expect to see some strategic use of DRS.
With the possibility of safety cars, teams will need to be flexible with their strategy and ready to react to changing conditions.
The high temperatures will put a strain on the engines, so reliability will be a key concern for the teams.
A well-timed undercut could be a game-changer here, allowing drivers to gain track position in the pits.
The wind can also play a significant role, affecting the car's balance and making it difficult to predict tire degradation.
